items.title: '카지노 견조한 성장' 파라다이스, 3분기 영업익 62%↑(종합)

items.title: 삼성 EUV 블랭크마스크 조달 비상…日호야 "더 못 늘린다"
items.snippet: 삼성전자의 내년 극자외선(EUV) 블랭크마스크 조달에 비상이 걸렸다. 10일 업계에 따르면 삼성전자 반도체 구매조직은 지난 9월 내년 공정 상황을 시뮬레이션한 결과 EUV 블랭크마스크 사용량이 급증할 것으로 판단하고 일본 호야에 공급량 확대를 요청했다. 그러나 호야는 다른 반도체 제조사 수요도 크게 확대되고 있다며 삼성의 요청을 모두 수용하기 어렵다는 입장을 전달했다.디일렉 취재를 종합하면 삼성전자의 EUV 블랭크마스크 사용량은 올해 5500장 안팎이다. 향후 3년간 매년 25%가량 늘어난다는 것이 회사 내부 시뮬레이션 결과다.EU

items.title: 與, 의총서 '의무공개매수제' 보완 논의…"야당과 지속적 협의"

items.snippet: 가상자산 거래소 빗썸에서 일부 회원에게 서비스 이용 불가 안내가 잘못 표시돼 고객 불편이 빚어졌다.10일 업계에 따르면 이날 오후 한때 빗썸 홈페이지에 접속한 일부 회원에게 '외국인 회원은 서비스 이용이 불가능하다'는 문구가 표시됐다. 빗썸은 공지를 통해 서비스 업데이트 과정에서 일부 회원에게 잘못된 문구가 일시적으로 노출됐다고 밝혔다. 이어 "실제 서비스 이용과는 무관한 안내 문구 표시 오류"라며 "외부 해킹 시도 등과는 무관하다"고 설명했다. 현재 빗썸 서비스는 정상적으로 이용할 수 있다.

items.title: 경찰청 찾은 중수청장 “수사 핑퐁은 오해…국민 권익이 우선”

items.title: 특검, 경기교육감 선거 개표 위조 정황 포착…선관위 압수수색
items.snippet: 6·3 지방선거에서 벌어진 투표용지 부족 사태 등을 수사하는 선관위 특검팀(특별검사 이태한)이 경기도교육감 선거에서 선관위 직원이 개표 상황표를 위조한 정황을 확인했다고 밝혔다. 특검은 선거관리위원회에 압수수색에 나섰다.제9회 전국동시지방선거 투표용지 부족 사태 등을 수사 중인 선관위 특검팀은 10일 “제9회 전국동시지방선거 경기도교육감 선거와 관련해 경기도 광주시 선관위에서 발생한 개표 결과 오입력 사건을 살피던 중, 광주시 선관위 직원이 개표상황표를 은닉하고 위조하여 실제 개표 결과와 달라진 정황을 확인했다”고 밝혔다.특검팀은 선관위 직원이 개표상황표를 위조한 이후 사후에 해당 은닉·위조 사실을 숨기기 위해 경기 광주시선관위 차원의 조직적 개입이 있었는지 여부를 규명할 방침이다.이를 위해 특검팀은 법원으로부터 공직선거법 위반 등의 혐의로...

items.title: 국힘, 이틀째 청와대 앞 집결…"특검법 거부권 행사해야"
items.snippet: 국민의힘이 오늘(10일) 청와대 앞에서 의원총회를 열고 이재명 대통령에게 조작기소 특검법안에 대해 거부권을 행사할 것을 압박했습니다.특검법안 공포안의 내주 국무회의 상정을 앞두고 지난 주말 대규모 장외 집회에 이어 전날에는 청와대 앞 최고위를 여는 등 대국민 반대 여론전 수위를 연일 높여가는 모습입니다.장동혁 대표는 이날 의총에서 "이번 특검법은 감옥에 있어야 할 이재명을 꺼내기 위한 이재명 탈옥법"이라면서 "이 법에 대해 거부권이 행사되지 않는다면 대한민국 전체가 나서서 거부권을 행사해야 한다"고 목소리를 높였습니다.장 대표는 "다음 총선에서, 다음 대선에서 이재명 정권을 심판해 역사와 법의 심판대에 세울 수 있도록 ..

items.title: 이 대통령 "미 중간선거 이후 변수 대비…금융시장 동요 막아야"
items.snippet: 이재명 대통령은 오늘(10일) "미국의 중간선거 이후 대외 환경의 여러 가지 변화가 예상된다"며 "관계 부처는 예상되는 다양한 변수를 다각도로 분석해 상황별 대응책을 치밀하게 마련해달라"고 주문했습니다.이 대통령은 이날 청와대에서 주재한 국무회의에서 "대외적 불확실성이 국내 경제에 미칠 부정적 영향을 최소화하는 데 만전을 기해야 한다"며 이같이 밝혔습니다.구체적으로는 "미국과 국제 경제의 상황을 주시하면서 금융 시장이 동요하는 일이 없도록 모니터링을 강화하고 신속한 대응 체계를 잘 갖춰달라"고 주문했습니다.이어 "외풍에 휘둘리지 않으려면 기초 체력을 키우는 일도 꼭 필요하다. 반도체·인공지능 등 핵심 전략산업을 한층 정..

items.title: “바쁘면 안 와도 된다” 했는데…중수청장 4주째 국무회의 참석
items.snippet: 김지용 중대범죄수사청장이 10일 이재명 대통령이 주재한 국무회의에 참석했다. 지난달 20일부터 중수청장 취임 이후 4주 연속 출석이다. 이 대통령이 앞서 “억지로 올 필요는 없다”고 말했으나, 김 청장은 임명된 이후 열린 네 번의 국무회의에 모두 참석했다.김 청장은 이날 오전 국무회의가 열리기 전 이정현 공소청장 직무대행과 김종철 경찰청장 직무대행을 만나 인사를 나눴다. 김 청장이 국무회의에 처음 참석한 것은 지난달 20일이다. 그는 이 대통령으로부터 같은 달 19일 임명장을 받고 이튿날 곧바로 국무회의에 처음 배석했다. 역대 정부에서는 수사기관의 독립성을 존중해 수사기관장은 국무회의에 배석시키지 않았다. 하지만 이 대통령이 지난해 12월 각 부처 소속의 외청도 국무회의에 참석하라고 지시하면서 검찰총장·경찰청장 직무대행도 배석하기 시작했다....

items.title: 이용철, 공소취소에 “법-원칙대로”… “대통령 친분 결격사유 아냐”
items.snippet: 이재명 대통령이 기소된 사건의 공소취소 논란과 관련해 이용철 법무부 장관 후보자는 9일 “진상 규명에 집중하는 게 맞다”는 공식 입장을 처음으로 밝혔다. 후보자 지명 이후 첫 공개 발언에서 공소취소 논란과 관련해 선을 긋는 대신 ‘특검 수사를 통한 진상 규명’이라는 답을 내놓은 것. 이에 대해 야당은 “결국 공소취소를 위한 수순이 시작됐다”고 반발했다. 한 전직 검사장도 “법무부 장관 후보자가 특검 조사가 필요하다고 인정한 셈”이라며 “공소취소 안 하겠다고 선을 안 그은 것 자체가 답변 아니겠느냐”고 지적했다.● 전임 장관·낙마 후보자 ‘공소취소’ 선 그었지만… 이 후보자는 조작기소 특검이 먼저 진상 규명을 한 뒤 “나머지 일은 법과 원칙에 따라 하는 것이 바람직하다”고 밝혔다. 더불어민주당 주도로 국회 본회의에서 통과된 조작기소 특검법은 윤...

items.title: 與 “李후보자, 개혁역량 쌓은 숨은 실력자”… ‘대장동 사업 설계자’ 野공세 차단 총력전
items.snippet: 더불어민주당이 이용철 법무부 장관 후보자를 ‘대장동 사업 설계자’로 지목한 야권의 공세를 차단하며 총력 방어전에 돌입했다. 국민의힘은 이른바 ‘성남 라인’인 이 후보자가 대장동 개발 의혹의 핵심 인물인 유동규 씨가 2010년 경기 성남시 시설관리공단 기획본부장으로 임용될 당시 추천위원이었던 것을 두고 ‘대장동 의혹의 숨은 설계자’라고 주장하며 지명 철회를 요구하고 있다. 민주당 김성회 원내대변인은 9일 유튜브 ‘민주당TV’에서 이 후보자가 지난달 방위사업청장 자격으로 출석했던 국회 국방위원회 국정감사를 언급하며 “문제 있는 인물이었으면 무려 20조 원의 예산을 다루는 방사청장을 (국민의힘이) 왜 가만뒀느냐”며 “성남에 주소지만 걸쳐도 뭐든지 할 수 있다고 생각하고 유튜브식 의혹 제기를 막 하는 것”이라고 비판했다. 민주당 내에선 현 정부 초대...

items.title: 野 “이용철, 경기 광주 농지에 불법 컨테이너” 李측 “적법”
items.snippet: 이용철 법무부 장관 후보자가 보유한 경기 광주시 농지에 대한 건축법 및 공직자윤리법 위반 의혹이 제기됐다. 농지에 컨테이너 박스 1동을 무단으로 설치하고 공직자 재산 신고를 허위로 한 정황이 있다는 게 야당의 주장이다. 국민의힘 주진우 의원은 9일 서울 여의도 국회에서 기자회견을 열고 “이 후보자는 경기 광주시 봉현리 농지에 불법 컨테이너 1동을 무단 설치해 건축법을 위반했고, 방위사업청장으로서 재산등록을 하면서 동식물 관련 시설이 있는 ‘건물과 대지’로 허위 신고했다”고 주장했다. 주 의원에 따르면 이 후보자는 2021년 5월 이 농지를 7000만 원에 매입했고, 해당 농지에는 녹슨 컨테이너 건물 1채만 있을 뿐 한국토지주택공사 부동산종합정보지도에 등재된 건물이 없다. 이 후보자는 또 이 땅과 맞붙어 있는 전원주택과 대지를 2016년 매입한...

items.title: 李, 소방공무원들과 오찬
items.snippet: 이재명 대통령이 9일 세종시에서 열린 ‘제64회 소방의 날 기념식’을 마친 뒤 윤호중 행정안전부 장관(오른쪽 앞), 소방공무원들과 격려 오찬을 하면서 사진을 찍기 위해 엄지손가락을 치켜세우고 있다. 이 대통령은 기념식에서 “대한민국 소방은 생명을 구해내며 작은 신의 역할을 대신하는 영웅”이라고 말했다.

items.title: “稅 부담 높이는 개편안, 전세시장 불안 키울수도”
items.snippet: 비거주 1주택자의 세 부담을 높이는 부동산 세제 개편안이 전세시장 불안을 키울 수 있다는 지적이 나왔다. 세 부담이 커진 집주인이 전세를 거둬들이고 직접 입주해 전세 매물 부족을 부추길 수 있다는 취지다. 9일 국회예산정책처가 개최한 2026년 세법 개정안 토론회에서 최한수 경북대 경제통상학부 교수는 “거주 여부에 따라 5억 원 정도의 양도소득세 부담 차이가 발생하면 실거주를 장려하는 것을 떠나 전세를 거둬들이고 입주할 유인이 생긴다”며 “전세시장이 취약한 시기에 이 제도를 도입하는 효과를 고민해볼 필요가 있다”고 말했다. 정부는 1주택자 양도세 장기보유특별공제에 10억 원 한도를 신설하고, 실제 거주한 기간이 짧을수록 공제 혜택을 줄이는 방안을 추진하고 있다. 장기간 보유했더라도 직접 거주하지 않은 1주택자는 양도세 부담이 커질 수 있다....

items.title: The Weight Is in the Reading: Hidden States in Memristors, Memlumors, and Electrochemical Transistors
items.abstract: Physical synapses are routinely described by a single number, the weight, that is identified with a conductance, a current, or a luminescence yield. This identification conflates two different objects: the internal state that the device stores, and the signal obtained when that state is read. Building on Chua's formulation of memristive systems, we separate the state variable, which evolves with the excitation history, from the observation map that converts it into a measured signal, and we define the weight as the outcome of a specified read protocol. Three platforms show the consequences: a memristor, in which the same voltage writes and reads; a memlumor, in which light both modifies the state and produces the photoluminescence that reports it; and an organic electrochemical transistor (OECT), in which the gate writes and the channel reads. items.title: Ground-state phase diagram of the spin-1/2 Heisenberg zigzag ladder with anisotropic $Γ$ term revisited
items.abstract: We study the spin-1/2 Heisenberg antiferromagnet with an anisotropic $Γ$ term on a zigzag ladder, which can be exactly mapped to the spin-1/2 XYZ zigzag ladder by a spin rotation. This model has recently attracted considerable interest as an effective model for the quasi-one-dimensional magnetic semiconductor YbCuS$_2$. For the model, the ground-state phase diagram was previously proposed by Saito and Hotta [Phys. Rev. Lett. 132, 166701 (2024); Phys. Rev. B 110, 024409 (2024)]. We systematically reexamine the phase diagram through complementary numerical and analytical approaches, including exact diagonalization, the density-matrix renormalization group method, and low-energy effective theories. We thereby demonstrate that when the anisotropic $Γ$ term is present, the model exhibits the Néel, dimer, ferromagnetic, and double-Néel phases, all of which have a finite excitation gap. The gap...

items.title: Neutronic Field-Effect Transistor
items.abstract: Field-effect electronic devices are in widespread use in communication, computing, data storage, and sensing applications. We demonstrate a neutronic field-effect transistor (NFET) that is analogous to the Datta-Das electron spin transistor and atomtronic devices. The NFET is based on a perfect-crystal Mach-Zehnder neutron interferometer with phase shifts applied to the spin and path degrees of freedom.

items.title: 특검이 ‘사건 왜곡’ 근거 만들면… 법무장관이 공소취소 지휘 가능성

items.title: 피해자가 새 증거 찾아도… 검사 “직접 못 받아” 경찰 “손 떠난 사건”
items.snippet: 사귀던 남성에게 스토킹과 협박을 당한 A씨는 남성이 기소된 후 과거 자신을 협박했던 통화 내역을 추가로 발견했다. A씨는 이 통화 내역을 법정에 추가 증거로 내려 했지만 난관에 부딪쳤다. 예전 같으면 검사에게 내면 됐다. 하지만 지난달 2일 시행된 개정 형사소송법은 검사가 피고인의 유죄 증거를 법원에 내지 못하도록 하고 있다. 경찰에 보완수사를 요구하거나, 피해자가 경찰에 낸 증거를 추송(追送·추후 송부)받아 법원에 내야 한다. A씨 증거를 경찰이 추송해야 해 재판은 2주 이상 지연됐다. A씨 변호인인 곽아량 변호사는 “본래 4주 뒤 재판인데 증거 제출 과정을 거치느라 6주 뒤로 잡았다”며 “검사도 피해자도 모두 답답한 상황”이라고 했다.

items.title: Spin-valve effect through electrostatic coupling
items.abstract: We propose a spin-valve effect in which an insulating magnetic van der Waals multilayer controls the conductance of an adjacent non-magnetic conductor by electrostatic coupling, without transport-electrons entering the magnetic layers. The coupling is induced by the variations of the electronic structure when the relative orientation of the magnetization of adjacent monolayers changes from parallel to antiparallel, modifying both the dielectric constant and band alignment. We consider two types of coupling and device concepts: charge transfer to a graphene monolayer and capacitive coupling in a single-electron transistor. items.title: Gate-tunable supercurrent switching in a three-terminal quantum dot transistor
items.abstract: We propose and analyze a three-terminal superconducting transistor switch in which a gate-defined quantum dot region interrupts a flux-controlled loop. The output supercurrent is switched off completely when the two loop arms couple to the dot with equal tunneling strengths and half a flux quantum threads the loop. The device then operates as a symmetric SQUID at half flux. The condition follows from a single geometric factor $χ$, which reduces the three-terminal problem to an equivalent two-terminal Anderson impurity model and makes the switching mechanism independent of the Coulomb interaction, the dot level position, the total hybridization and temperature. These enter only through a prefactor and thus decide how tolerant the device is to imperfect barrier tuning. items.title: Defects and Structural Evolution in CrSBr: Machine-Learning Potentials for Atomistic Simulations
items.abstract: The layered van der Waals semiconductor CrSBr combines intrinsic magnetic order with semiconducting and optical properties, making it a promising material for multifunctional electronic and photonic applications. Understanding how defects and structural transformations affect its properties under experimentally relevant conditions, however, remains challenging for first-principles simulations due to the relevant length and time scales. Here, we develop and benchmark machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) for the Cr-S-Br system, enabling large-scale atomistic simulations of CrSBr with accuracy approaching that of density functional theory (DFT). The charge-aware variant qNEP achieves near-DFT accuracy in predicting lattice constants, formation enthalpies, vacancy energetics, and the anisotropic pressure response of o-CrSBr. items.title: 靑 "조작기소 특검법, 다음 주 국무회의 상정 예정"
Impact of multi-dot configurations on electron temperature and double quantum dot latching in gate-controlled qubit devices
items.abstract: Many currently envisaged scalable architectures for Si/SiGe spin qubit devices utilize gate-controlled multi-dot configurations characterized by their peculiar Coulomb blockade physics. One example is the concurrent use of a single electron transistor (SET) as a charge sensor and as a reservoir for adjacent qubit quantum dots (QD). We find that the SET energy spectrum impacts pulsed gate spectroscopy of the QD when the SET simultaneously acts as the reservoir and the sensor. Then, using the qubit QD as a probe, we quantify how strongly the electron temperature of the SET depends on the applied bias. It surpasses a reference experiment by 100 $mK$ even at 50 $μV$ bias. Our results provide a strong incentive for choosing spin qubit initialization schemes which do not rely on coupling to the reservoir in such devices. items.title: Environmental Assessment of GaN Current-Source and Voltage-Source AC-AC Variable Speed Drives
items.abstract: Three-phase ac-ac converters for variable-speed drives can be realized conventionally as voltage-source converters (VSCs) or, leveraging emerging monolithic bidirectional GaN power transistors (M-BDSs), as current-source converters (CSCs). This paper presents a comparative life-cycle assessment of a realized VSC and a CSC demonstrators including grid-side and motor-side EMI filters, and with identical specifications (1.4 kW rated power, 200 V line-to-line rms grid and motor voltage). The embodied carbon footprints are similar (44.8 kgCO2eq for the VSC and 47.4 kgCO2eq for the CSC) and dominated by auxiliary and control electronics, and the printed circuit boards. items.title: Rapid Heat Removal from Chip Cores: Near-Junction Active Cooling of Power Transistors via Electron Entropy Transport and Spatial Decoupling
items.abstract: Chip performance is limited by a shared bottleneck: the core produces heat faster than it can be moved out. We study the hardest case, RF power GaN HEMTs, whose hotspots exceed 5 kW/cm^2, and propose a horizontal near-junction active cooling topology built on electron entropy transport. Classical on-chip thermoelectric cooling faces a contest: Peltier absorption grows linearly with current, Joule heating with its square. In a vertical pillar, its own conduction resistance locks about half the Joule heat back toward the cold end, capping net cooling. From the Onsager framework we show the origin of this asymmetry: Peltier absorption localizes at the interface where the Seebeck coefficient jumps, whereas Joule heating fills the volume. items.title: Orbital texture of valence band and interband transitions of the type-II multiferroic van der Waals NiI$_2$
items.abstract: NiI$_2$ is a van der Waals semiconductor characterized by complex electronic and magnetic phases, holding promise towards functional applications. For this purpose, a detailed understanding of its band structure and its excitations is essential to elucidate the electronic and transport properties. We present a comprehensive description of the band structure and of the lowest valence-to-conduction band transition in bulk NiI$_2$, by means of time- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy supported by first-principles calculations. We describe the orbital character of Ni and I manifolds, and identify the main momentum-resolved features of the valence band and the shallow minima of the conduction band. With this study, we provide a foundational understanding of the electronic structure of NiI$_2$ and its single-particle interband electronic excitation, a benchmark for theoretical model...

items.title: A Per-Step Load-Balancing Engine for Expert-Parallel MoE Serving
items.abstract: In expert-parallel Mixture-of-Experts serving, a layer finishes only when the most loaded GPU of its group does. Token routing shifts at every decode step and concentrates on a few experts, so most of the group's reserved GPU time waits on stragglers. Recovering that time means re-deciding, at every layer of every decode step, how each replicated expert's tokens divide between its copies. The exact linear-program solvers that make this decision optimally take longer than many of the layers they serve, and their working set outgrows GPU shared memory at deployment scale. We introduce Relief, a bidirectional pairwise relaxation that makes the linear program unnecessary, coming within a fraction of a point of the per-step optimum in a few passes of integer halving over the token counts. We build and measure three deployments, CUDA kernels on the serving GPU, the same verified engine on an F...

items.title: $>3\text{ W/mm}$ Output Power $\mathrm{Al}_{0.61}\mathrm{Ga}_{0.39}\mathrm{N}$ Channel HEMT with $24.4\%$ Associated PAE at $10\text{ GHz}$
items.abstract: In this work, an ultra-wide bandgap (UWBG) high-electron-mobility transistor (HEMT) was fabricated using an $\mathrm{Al}_{0.76}\mathrm{Ga}_{0.24}\mathrm{N}$ barrier and an $\mathrm{Al}_{0.61}\mathrm{Ga}_{0.39}\mathrm{N}$ channel with thick $\mathrm{SiO}_2$ passivation. The device demonstrated low current collapse at $40\text{ V}$ drain bias. At $10\text{ GHz}$, the device exhibited an output power of $3.07\text{ W/mm}$ with an associated power-added efficiency (PAE) of $24.4\%$. A peak PAE of $33.9\%$ was achieved at an associated output power of $2.14\text{ W/mm}$. This excellent large-signal performance highlights the strong potential of UWBG $\mathrm{AlGaN}$ channel devices for X-band applications.

The devices featured a recessed T-gate structure and $\mathrm{SiO_2}$ passivation. Scaled devices achieved a cutoff frequency ($f_{\mathrm{T}}$) of 35 GHz, a maximum oscillation frequency ($f_{\mathrm{max}}$) of 82 GHz, and an average breakdown field $> 3 \mathrm{MV/cm}$, while maintaining a reasonable current collapse of $\sim 20\%$ under a 40 V drain bias in pinch-off condition. Devices with larger dimensions demonstrated a high off-state breakdown voltage of 883 V and an $f_{\mathrm{T}}$ of 24 GHz, yielding a high Johnson's figure of merit ($\mathrm{JFOM}$) of 21.19 $\mathrm{THz \cdot V}$. items.title: Deterministically fabricated C-band single-photon sources based on quantum dot circular Bragg grating cavities
items.abstract: Telecom-wavelength quantum light sources are essential components for scalable fiber-based quantum networks, where on-demand emission of single photons is required for high secret key rates. Here, we demonstrate the deterministic integration of metal-organic vapor-phase epitaxy (MOVPE)-grown C-band InAs/InP quantum dots into circular Bragg grating resonators. The integrated emitters exhibit a radiative lifetime of $T_1 = (1400 \pm 50)~\mathrm{ps}$ and a spectral linewidth of $ΔE_{\mathrm{FWHM}} = (41.0 \pm 4.0)~μ\mathrm{eV}$. Under non-resonant excitation, we measure a post-selected single-photon purity of $(0.95 \pm 0.02)$ and a raw two-photon interference visibility of $V_{12\mathrm{ns}} = (35 \pm 2)\%$, which increases to $(70 \pm 18)\%$ under temporal post-selection. items.title: Fabrication and Characterization of Flexible In2O3 Thin-Film Transistors on Mica Substrates
items.abstract: Flexible oxide-semiconductor thin-film transistors (TFTs) with high field-effect mobility (uFE > 70 cm^2/Vs) are required for next-generation flexible displays. Polycrystalline In2O3-based TFTs are promising candidates; however, conventional flexible substrates such as plastics are not suitable because their fabrication typically requires relatively high temperatures (~350 deg.C). In this study, we used mica as a flexible substrate to fabricate polycrystalline In2O3-based TFTs, motivated by previous demonstrations of crystalline oxide growth on mica. The resulting TFTs exhibited a uFE of approximately 75 cm^2/Vs. The devices maintained gate-modulated operation after 10^3 flex-out bending cycles at a 5 mm radius, whereas flex-in cycling caused early electrical failure, likely due to In2O3 film degradation. The TFTs also operated normally after exposure to 85 deg.C and 40% relative humidit...

items.title: The World Model Planning Accelerator (WMPA): Hardware-Algorithm Co-Design for Embedded AI in Robotics
items.abstract: Embedded AI is moving from perception to prediction. Robots now use world models$\unicode{x2014}$learned simulators that predict the outcome of candidate actions in a compressed latent space before any is executed. Every predicted step must be computed on board within a tight power and thermal budget, yet the energy these steps fundamentally require, and how far real hardware sits from it, have not been characterized. We derive lower bounds on the arithmetic operations and the CMOS dynamic energy of a latent state transition from information theory and Boolean circuit complexity. Profiling a DreamerV3-style Recurrent State Space Model (RSSM) shows that every rollout operation is memory-bandwidth bound and that a GPU consumes at least $5.9\times10^{10}$ times the CMOS energy floor. items.title: How light interacts with matter, revisited
items.abstract: In 1968 Victor Weisskopf explained in Scientific American how light interacts with matter, with a few formulas and many words. We tell the same story again with the tools that have since become available: the fields are computed and drawn, and their evolution in time is shown in animations. Light is described as a classical electromagnetic field and matter as a collection of charged oscillators; every phenomenon follows from adding up the retarded waves radiated by the oscillators, each with its proper delay and phase. items.abstract: Surface oxidation plays an important role in governing charge transport in semiconductor nanoparticle assemblies. Here, we investigate the optoelectronic properties of solution-processed tellurium (Te) nanoparticle ensembles prepared through gradual ambient-air exposure. Structural and spectroscopic analyses reveal interconnected elemental Te nanoparticles with coexisting alpha-TeO2 and hydroxyl-containing surface species, exhibiting a lower relative contribution of oxidized Te than previously investigated forced-air-oxidized ensembles. The resulting photodetectors demonstrate photoresponse at 405, 532, and 1550 nm, with maximum responsivities of 10.1, 14.4, and 8.5 mA/W, respectively. items.title: Trajectory-Dependent Decoherence and Leakage During Shuttling of Multi-Spin Qubits
items.abstract: Logical qubits encoded in collective states of multiple spins are promising building blocks for large-scale semiconductor quantum processors. As novel fault-tolerant architectures increasingly rely on qubit shuttling, understanding decoherence of the shuttled multi-spin qubits becomes crucial. We analyze fidelity and leakage of the logical qubits dephased by the spatio-temporally correlated $1/f$ noise, considering two-, three-, and four-spin encodings. We study different shuttling protocols and establish that for all encodings generally, parallel shuttling provides the best protection against decoherence at short distances, whereas sequential shuttling outperforms others for long-range transport (although the exact boundaries depend on the specific device parameters). items.title: Discrete time crystals and heteroclinic switching in actively mode-locked semiconductor lasers
items.abstract: We investigate the mechanisms underlying the emergence of discrete time crystals in actively mode-locked semiconductor lasers. Our analysis is based on a Haus master equation generalized to retain carrier memory between round-trips. We perform a detailed bifurcation analysis that reveals a well-defined hierarchy of subharmonic states, illustrating how pulses may suppress their neighbors when the modulation runs faster than the pulse round-trip frequency. To identify the underlying mechanism, we derive effective equations of motion that couple the pulse energies, their positions relative to the modulation transmission maxima, and the local time-dependent gain. These reveal that transitions between time-crystalline states occur via transcritical global bifurcations, opening a regime of heteroclinic winnerless competition between symmetry-degenerate configurations.

items.title: Microscopic theory of exciton polarons in transition metal dichalcogenides
items.abstract: Polarons are composite quasiparticles formed when charge carriers strongly couple to lattice vibrations, manifesting as carriers dressed by a surrounding cloud of phonons. Although this dressing fundamentally renormalizes the effective mass and mobility of carriers, its impact on electrically neutral exciton polarons in 2D semiconductors has received limited attention. In particular, despite the growing interest in polaronic effects in atomically thin semiconductors, only a few theoretical studies have addressed spectral signatures and renormalized properties of exciton polarons in these materials. Here, we develop a microscopic model to describe exciton polarons in transition metal dichalcogenides. items.title: Exciton design via topological spin textures
items.abstract: Excitons carry energy and information through a semiconductor without carrying charge. This makes them attractive for optoelectronics, but also hard to guide. Magnetic skyrmions, on the other hand, are moved by small electrical currents. Here we develop a theory of excitons interacting with a skyrmion in which the electron and the hole are treated as distinct constituents, each with its own spin--orbit coupling. We find that the topology of the skyrmion is transferred to the exciton only when the exchange coupling exceeds the relevant spin--orbit splitting. The exciton then experiences a full flux quantum, with opposite signs in the two valleys. The quantum metric of the spin texture creates a ring-shaped barrier that traps excitons, whereas the topological charge fixes the angular momentum of the trapped states and hence their optical selection rules. items.abstract: High-precision astrometry is a cornerstone for detecting Earth-like exoplanets in the habitable zones of nearby solar-type stars and probing the nature of dark matter in galactic environments. Achieving sub-microarcsecond accuracy requires unprecedented control over detector morphology, optical distortion, and astrometric measurement techniques. This paper reviews recent progress in characterizing large format detector at the micropixel scale level, calibrating optical distortion using reference stars, and refining differential astrometry methods to detect the faint astrometric signatures of Earth-mass exoplanets. We highlight the latest developments in the RETINA project, which aims to advance the TRL of GIGAPYX 220 MP CMOS detectors from Pyxalis which are critical components for future space missions such as ESA's Theia and NASA's Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO). items.title: On the collective flow puzzle in ultra-central heavy-ion collisions
items.abstract: Using UCC-DiffHIC, an AI-accelerated event-by-event hydrodynamic model validated against hybrid simula- tions, we study flow in ultracentral Pb-Pb collisions. For suitable initial conditions, the calculated v2{2}/v3{2} approaches unity in the most central collisions, consistent with experiment. An exact response decomposition shows that residual fluctuations suppress the ratio through P3/P2 < 1, where P2 and P3 are Pearson response correlations for elliptic and triangular flow, respectively. This resolves the apparent flow hierarchy without requiring a breakdown of linear response or additional effects such as nuclear deformation.

items.title: Inverse design of superconductors and semiconductors with differentiable foundation models
items.abstract: Designing a crystal for a target property requires choosing its elements, stoichiometry, and atomic structure together, yet gradients exist only for the continuous structural variables. We introduce differentiable Equiformer fast effective-atom theory (DEFEAT), which lets a pretrained EquiformerV3 foundation model accept continuous species weights and site occupancies without retraining on fractional data, thereby enabling gradient-based materials optimization. Gradients from fine-tuned property models and a machine-learned energy penalty then guide updates to composition, atom count, atomic positions, and lattice vectors in a single optimization. items.title: High-Volume Wurtzite MnSe in MnSe/CdSe Superlattices: Structure, Magnetism and Optical Response
items.abstract: Polymorphism in Mn-based chalcogenides offers access to magnetic semiconductors with distinct crystal symmetries, polar structures, and different magnetic orders. In particular, wurtzite MnSe exhibits an appealing interplay of electric polarization and several competing magnetic phases including altermagnetic order. However, stabilizing metastable polymorphs, such as wurtzite MnSe, in experimentally useful volumes remains challenging. Here, we show that a nanoscale-period MnSe/CdSe superlattice stabilizes wurtzite MnSe over micrometer-scale total thickness while suppressing the formation of the thermodynamically favored rock-salt phase. The increased magnetic volume enables bulk-sensitive characterization of this polar polymorph. items.title: Topology as a Design Variable: Joint Architecture-Sizing Optimization for SRAM
items.abstract: SRAM's power-performance-area-stability trade-off depends on bitcell topology, a discrete architectural choice that interacts non-separably with continuous transistor sizing. However, no open-source SRAM tool treats topology as an optimizable variable. OpenRAM generates SRAM layouts but performs no optimization, while OpenYield supports high-fidelity evaluation but restricts optimization to scalar sizing of a fixed 6T cell. OpenYieldV2 closes this gap through three integrated contributions. First, a fully parameterized compiler generates complete 6T and 10T SRAM macros with peripheral circuits and replica-bitline self-timing, enabling topology comparison under identical simulation conditions. Second, a few-shot TabPFN surrogate learns topology-dependent PPA responses with limited full-macro SPICE samples. items.title: Strong phonon-coupled trion emission in Janus homobilayer
items.abstract: Janus transition metal dichalcogenides with broken mirror symmetry provide a novel platform for exploring many-body effects mediated by spin-valley-phonon interactions. Strong electron-phonon coupling demands a precise match between a strong effective dipole moment and nanometer-scale charge confinement. Here, we report thermally robust and enhanced trion emission in a symmetric bilayer WSeS with an S/S stacking configuration. The inward-pointing antiparallel built-in electric fields induce a strong electron confinement effect at the interface, driving dominant trion emission at cryogenic temperatures. Furthermore, a massive electron-phonon coupling strength (3.9) resonant with the optical phonon A_1^2 energy (51 meV) contributes to the thermal stability of this trion emission at elevated temperatures. items.title: FoundaRF: A Physics-Informed Foundation Model Framework for Radio-Frequency Passive Components
items.abstract: Designing RF/mmWave passive components is a time-consuming process that relies heavily on expert knowledge and iterative EM simulations. Although recent ML surrogate models have shown great promise in accelerating passive design, they remain task-specific and lack generalization. This paper presents FoundaRF, a foundation model framework that unifies passive layout modeling across diverse layout structures and technologies. It combines a self-supervised encoder with adaptive layout processing and physics-aware decoders to enable few-shot transfer. Experiments across four semiconductor technologies show strong generalization to unseen structures, outperforming baselines with up to a 3.3x reduction in prediction error, reducing labeled-data requirements by up to fourfold, and substantially shortening design turnaround. items.title: Deep-UV All-dielectric qBIC Metasurface for Refractive Index Sensing
items.abstract: All-dielectric metasurfaces supporting quasi-bound states in the continuum (qBICs) have emerged as powerful platforms for biosensing, yet their operation remains largely concentrated in the visible and near-infrared regimes. Extending these resonances into the deep-ultraviolet (DUV) to probe the intrinsic electronic absorption of biomolecules presents substantial material and nanofabrication challenges. Here, we experimentally demonstrate a hafnium dioxide (HfO$_{2}$) metasurface supporting DUV qBICs in the wavelength range from 225 nm to 340 nm with quality factors reaching 500. We further demonstrate its refractive index sensing capabilities through integration with a microfluidic cell and optical characterization in reflection mode. We show that the introduction of an aqueous buffer leads to a further quality factor enhancement. Achieving a sensitivity of up to approximately 60 nm/RIU...

items.title: Hybrid integration of a SESAM with a silicon nitride photonic integrated circuit
items.abstract: The realization of high-performance femtosecond lasers on photonic integrated circuits (PICs) requires robust, low-loss coupling between a saturable absorber and a photonic waveguide. In this work, we demonstrate the hybrid integration of a semiconductor saturable absorber mirror (SESAM) with a silicon nitride (SiN) PIC by micro-assembly. This micro-assembly strategy transfers the non-linear functionality of the absorber onto the PIC. We characterize the linear and non-linear performance of an unbonded SESAM and of a SESAM bonded to inverse-tapered SiN waveguides. At 1560~nm, the bonded device shows a waveguide-coupled modulation depth of 5.2\%, a maximum reflectivity of 37.2\%, and a saturation fluence of 47~\textmu J/cm$^2$. This work demonstrates that SESAMs can be integrated directly onto silicon nitride-based PIC platforms and provides a pathway towards fully integrated, self-starti...

items.title: Experimental demonstration of dual-polarization nonreciprocal thermal emission at moderate magnetic fields
items.abstract: Conventional thermal emitters obey Kirchhoff's law of thermal radiation, which requires emissivity and absorptivity to be equal at each wavelength, angle, and polarization. This in turn places a fundamental limit on a range of radiative energy technologies as well as heat transfer. This constraint can however be overcome using magneto-optic semiconductors, which break Lorentz reciprocity under an applied magnetic field. However, in most prior experimental demonstrations, nonreciprocity has been restricted to TM polarization, since the electric field of TE-polarized light is parallel to the applied magnetic field. items.abstract: Kinetic equations in the high-field regime describe particle transport dominated by electric-field acceleration and collisional relaxation. These equations are widely used in simulations of plasmas and semiconductor devices. Typical models include the Vlasov--Poisson--Fokker--Planck (VPFP) and Boltzmann--Poisson systems. Their high dimensionality and multiscale nature pose two of the major challenges to accurate and efficient numerical solution. To address these challenges, we propose an asymptotic-preserving tensor neural network (APTNN) method. Specifically, to reduce high-dimensional computational costs and memory requirements, we adopt the canonical polyadic (CP) decomposition structure of TNNs to approximate their solutions. items.abstract: Parametric amplifiers are a workhorse for near-quantum-limited measurements above 1 GHz. However, amplifier development has been more limited below 1 GHz. We present a kinetic inductance traveling-wave parametric amplifier (KI-TWPA) operating over 300-700 MHz, with gain exceeding 30 dB and pump powers of a few hundred nanowatts. items.title: Electrostatics of Chern junctions in a magnetic field
items.abstract: Electrostatic control is central to the operation of semiconductor junctions made from conventional materials. Here, we theoretically investigate the electrostatic properties of lateral junctions between two-dimensional (2D) Chern semiconductors in a perpendicular magnetic field. The spectral asymmetry of a Chern semiconductor acts as a magnetic-field-induced effective dopant density that is dependent on the Chern number. As a consequence, two regions with different Chern numbers acquire different chemical potentials at charge neutrality, leading to a built-in potential of topological origin across the junction. Using this built-in potential as a boundary condition, we solve the 2D Poisson equation to obtain the electric potential and charge density profiles, as well as the capacitance, of Chern semiconductor junctions. items.title: Parabolic Extrapolation of Compactness with Applications to Characterizations of the Parabolic CMO Space via Parabolic Fractional Commutators

items.abstract: Extreme events often occur sequentially, from earthquake-tsunami cascades to successive extreme losses in financial markets. We introduce an extremal token representation that encodes multivariate observations as a categorical sequence. The representation is invariant to componentwise strictly increasing transformations. It preserves the identity and temporal ordering of dominant exceedances but discards their magnitudes and the identities of nondominant simultaneous exceedances. items.title: Optical Ceiling on Polaron Mobility in Disordered Molecular Semiconductors: Lessons from Eumelanin
items.abstract: Polaron hopping in disordered molecular semiconductors such as eumelanin is set by energetic disorder $σ$ and reorganization energy $λ$. We show that the reduced polaron absorption band encodes this transport problem. Its value at zero energy fixes the mean hop rate, which bounds the mobility in any dimension. For Gaussian disorder and classical vibrations its centroid is $E_\mathrm{op}=λ+(1-c)σ^2/k_BT$, its variance obeys the Hush relation, and the bound is the Marcus rate at $λ\to E_\mathrm{op}$; a 1D lower bound vanishes at $k_BT^*=(1-c)σ^2/λ$, read from optics.

The framework enables efficient quantitative treatment of carrier nonlocality, carrier surface accumulation and depletion, and nonlocal damping in three-dimensional semiconductor nanostructures, under electrical tuning and across a wide range of doping densities. items.title: Cage-enforced i-wave altermagnetism in boron-carbon clathrates
items.abstract: The spin splitting of an altermagnet arises from a rotation that relates its two magnetic sublattices. In known cases it is fixed by the crystal structure. Here we show that guest-host frameworks separate the two roles. In the boron-carbon clathrates $M$B$_3$C$_3$ the ordered cage removes the translation between the two guest sites and enforces cubic $i$-wave altermagnetism, with six symmetry-enforced nodal planes, for any magnetic guest in the compensated state; strain retunes the class to $d$- or $g$-wave. We demonstrate the platform with GdB$_3$C$_3$: its compensated antiferromagnetic ground state is a narrow-gap semiconductor with spin splitting of 0.19 eV at the conduction-band edge, and its weakly pinned Néel vector switches the helicity-resolved optical response on and off according to the magnetic point group. Thermodynamic stability at high pressure and dynamical stability at am...

items.title: Current-Confined Formation of a Buried Ge/Si Free Surface for Defect Filtering
items.abstract: Lattice-mismatched heteroepitaxy is limited by misfit dislocations, threading defects, and residual strain generated at buried interfaces. Here, we show that current-confined electrochemistry transforms the Ge/Si heterointerface into a laterally continuous nanometric free surface while preserving the Ge epilayer. A low-doped Ge layer on a conductive p-type Si substrate redirects anodization current toward the misfit-dislocation-rich interface. Numerical modelling including charge-transfer kinetics shows that this confinement arises from hole-limited charge transfer and, together with electrochemical calibration, defines a process window that combines interfacial current confinement with controlled Si porosification. STEM reveals an approximately 15 Ang separation, while EDX shows localized interfacial oxygen enrichment. After soft annealing, geometric phase analysis and plan-view TEM sho...

items.title: Universal model of the growth of III-V tetrahedral semiconductors on polar surfaces: pyramids and glue atoms. VII. Step kinetics
items.abstract: Ab initio calculations were used to simulate the kinetics of attachment of new segments of the crystalline lattice (pyramids) at steps on the nonmetal-terminated surface of tetrahedral semiconductors: GaN, GaP, GaAs and GaSb. These surfaces are wurtzite gallium nitride, i.e. GaN(000-1) surface, zinc blende gallium phosphide, i.e. GaP(-1-1-1) gallium arsenide, GaAs(-1-1-1) and gallium antimonide GaSb(-1-1-1) surfaces. Diffusion species are gallium adatoms at high coverage or gallium adatoms connected with nonmetal atom creating stable pyramids. These pyramids arrive at the steps, and cannot be attached be directly because the Ga adatom at the pyramid base cannot be attached directly. Therefore they are incorporated into the step by additional nonmetal atoms glue atoms arriving from the vapor or detached from other segments of the surface terraces.

items.abstract: Ab initio calculations were used to simulate surface diffusion of adsorbates on the nonmetal-terminated surface of tetrahedral semiconductors: GaN, GaP, GaAs and GaSb. These surfaces are wurtzite gallium nitride, i.e. GaN(000-1) surface, zinc blende gallium phosphide, i.e. GaP(-1-1-1) gallium arsenide, GaAs (-1-1-1) and gallium antimonide GaSb (-1-1-1) surfaces. The mixed coverage consists of Ga adatoms in the first layer with a nonmetal atom attached above them forming a triangular-based pyramid. The pyramidal structures are stable during surface jumps involving rotations around one of the basal Ga adatoms. Thus, the diffusion proceeds via rotation (pivot) of the pair of the other basal Ga adatoms around an immobile Ga adatom moving them into new, originally empty sites. items.title: Cross-Domain Joint-Embedding Pretraining For Heterogeneous Industrial Time Series
items.abstract: Industrial predictive maintenance and manufacturing tasks frequently contain abundant sensor measurements, but with limited labeled data. We investigate cross-domain self-supervised pretraining using joint-embedding predictive architecture for heterogeneous industrial time series (JEPA-HITS), which learns one encoder from various domains such as battery, semiconductor chemical mechanical planarization (CMP), computer numerical control (CNC) machining, and bearing while preserving dataset-specific temporal scales. We evaluate representation reuse on regression and classification problems under reduced-label downstream training, and leave-one-domain-out (LODO) pretraining. Compared with the same architecture initialized randomly, LODO pretraining reduces RMSE from 10.72 to 7.95 on battery remaining useful life (RUL), 4.34 to 3.89 on CMP, and 13.53 to 11.72 on tool wear regression, while im...

items.title: Gate-tunable superconductor-semiconductor coupling and its impact on zero-energy modes in PbTe-Pb nanowires
items.abstract: Superconductor-semiconductor coupling in hybrid nanowires plays a pivotal role in Majorana devices. Here, we demonstrate this tunable coupling in PbTe-Pb nanowires and its impact on the induced gap and zero-bias peaks (ZBPs). In the strong coupling regime, the device reveals a clean superconducting gap, where robust and non-robust ZBPs are observed in distinct magnetic field ranges. Conversely, increasing the gate voltage drives the system toward the weak coupling regime, where the gap becomes narrow and soft. Consequently, robust ZBPs disappear while non-robust ones persist. Our results establish a direct link between tunable coupling and robust ZBPs, providing guidelines on engineering Majorana zero modes and topological qubits.

items.title: Amplification of valley polarization in an hBN-separated MoSe2-WSe2 heterostructure
items.abstract: Transition metal dichalcogenide heterostructures host long-lived interlayer excitons in the +K and -K valleys that can encode long-lived valley polarization. We investigated the low-temperature valley polarization dynamics in an MoSe2-bilayer hBN-WSe2 heterostructure. The bilayer hBN spacer results in an interlayer exciton lifetime exceeding 2 μs and an anomalous valley polarization amplification effect. Our theoretical model shows that this amplification results from the long exciton lifetime and exciton-exciton interactions. This work sets the stage for long-lived interlayer excitons to be used in nonlinear valleytronic transistors and amplifiers.

items.title: Optical Detection of Coefficient of Thermal Expansion via Frequency Tracking at Cryogenic Temperatures
items.abstract: Accurate characterization of the coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) in nanoscale thin films is critical for predicting residual stress and ensuring the reliability of modern micro-electromechanical systems and advanced semiconductor architectures. The primary limitation is that traditional methods depend on precise thickness measurements or are restricted to crystalline materials. In this work, we present an in-situ, non-destructive optical methodology to determine the CTE of suspended nanofilms by tracking the temperature-dependence of their vibrational frequency. This approach eliminates thickness measurements entirely and works for amorphous films where X-ray diffraction (XRD) fails. We experimentally validate this technique across a broad temperature range, evaluating membranes in their native microstructure state without requiring additional destructive patterning or complex sam...

items.title: Band Alignment of Grafted versus Directly Bonded Si/Ge Heterostructures
items.abstract: The electronic properties of semiconductor heterostructures are influenced by the local bonding and electrostatic environment at the heterointerface. Here, we investigate how the interface-formation mechanism modifies the band alignment of Si/Ge heterostructures by directly comparing Al2O3-mediated semiconductor grafting with direct bonding. Interface-sensitive X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy combined with Kraut analysis reveals type-I band alignment for both structures, but with different band offsets: the valence-band offset increases from ~0.08 eV for directly bonded Si/Ge to ~0.21 eV for grafted Si/Al2O3/Ge, accompanied by a corresponding reduction in the conduction-band offset. Raman spectroscopy further distinguishes the two interfacial configurations. The different core-level shifts and band offsets indicate that the electronic structure is sensitive to the interfacial bonding an...

items.title: Nondestructive 3D Metrology of Through-Glass Via Geometry and Internal Wall Texture Using Holotomography
items.abstract: Through-glass vias (TGVs) are increasingly important for semiconductor packaging, yet their internal geometry and wall texture remain difficult to characterize nondestructively. Here, we use holotomography (HT) to inspect the three-dimensional (3D) geometry and internal wall texture of intact, unfilled TGVs before metallization. HT reconstructs the refractive index (RI) distribution of the glass and via. Maps of RI and spatially filtered RI then localize the internal boundary. Geometric fitting quantifies via dimensions and taper, while spatial filtering separates slowly varying wall form from finer texture. The reconstructed surface supports volumetric visualization, dimensional measurements and spatial characterization of wall texture within one optical inspection workflow. These measurements reveal internal features inaccessible from surface views and provide quantitative descriptors...

items.title: Trapping photo-carriers in undoped gate-defined quantum dots using an on-chip microwave resonator for charge readout
items.abstract: Scaling up gate-defined quantum dot systems is hindered by the rapid growth in the number of control gates. To tackle this challenge, we propose a different approach where the quantum dots are created from optically generated charges trapped beneath accumulation gates. By shining an above-the-gap laser light onto an undoped GaAs substrate, we demonstrate that it is possible to create and separate electron-hole pairs to form quantum dots. For the charge readout, we use a superconducting coplanar waveguide resonator capacitively coupled to the quantum dots. With these elements, we demonstrate a working many-charge double quantum dot device comprised of only two plunger gates, one tunnel coupling gate and one sensing gate. These features have led to their widespread adoption in scintillator-based detectors for both fundamental and applied physics. In recent years, there has been a growing interest in the detection of scintillation light at cryogenic temperatures in low-temperature experiments based on bolometric detectors, such as RES-NOVA and CUPID, as well as in emerging quantum applications. In the RES-NOVA experiment, radiopure PbWO$_4$ crystals are used to detect supernova neutrinos. items.title: Self-driven beta-radiation detection through a graphene/water/silicon heterostructure
items.abstract: Large-volume neutrino observatories, exemplified by IceCube, exploit Cherenkov light generated by neutrino-induced charged particles in Antarctic ice, highlighting the potential of water-based media for high-energy particle detection. In $β$-decay, a neutron converts into a proton via the weak interaction, emitting an electron and an electron antineutrino. The electron constitutes the beta radiation detected in this work, while the accompanying antineutrino motivates future extensions toward neutrino detection. Here we demonstrate a complementary electrical transduction strategy using a graphene/water/silicon heterostructure that generates reversible current transients under beta irradiation at zero applied bias. items.title: Energy Transfer and Strong Coupling in Plasmonic Systems
items.abstract: The coupling between plasmon resonances of metal nanostructures and electronic excitations of molecular/semiconductor systems is important in a number of applications, including surface enhanced spectroscopy, hot-electron catalysis, plasmon-induced resonance energy transfer and the creation of hybrid light-matter states. The past several decades has seen a large number of experimental studies of these effects, as well as the development of theory to explain the results. In this Perspectives article we use classical electromagnetic (EM) simulations to examine how the localized surface plasmon resonances (LSPRs) of metal nanoparticles and propagating surface plasmon polaritons (SPPs) in extended metal nanostructures (wires/plates/films) are affected by interactions with a molecular/semiconductor system. The classical EM simulations are complemented by a quantum model for plasmon-exciton co...

items.title: Cross-Scale Spatial Reasoning: A Learning-Centered Framework for Designing Immersive Learning Environments
items.abstract: Understanding complex scientific and engineering systems often requires learners to connect structures, processes, and behaviors across different spatial scales and levels of organization. Although research on spatial cognition, scale, multiple representations, and systems thinking has examined aspects of this challenge, these perspectives do not always provide explicit guidance for designing learning activities that require learners to integrate information across levels. Immersive technologies offer opportunities to explore otherwise inaccessible structures, coordinate representations, and investigate system behavior, but their educational value depends on the reasoning they support. This paper proposes Cross-Scale Spatial Reasoning (CSSR) as an integrative framework for understanding how learners establish and use spatial and structural relationships across scales or organizational le...

items.title: Reasoning Across Scales: Learning Challenges and Opportunities for Immersive Technologies in Chip Design Education
items.abstract: As demand for semiconductor talent grows, education must prepare learners for the complexity of modern chip design. Instruction typically relies on lectures, textbooks, software exercises, and limited laboratory experiences. Although foundational, these approaches offer limited support for understanding the spatial, multi-scale, and interconnected nature of chip design. Virtual reality (VR) can help learners visualize and interact with complex structures and processes, but its educational opportunities remain underexplored. We examined this gap through chip design curriculum analysis and semi-structured interviews with five participants representing instructional and learner perspectives. We characterized four learning demands: descriptive knowledge, procedural knowledge, relational and design-focused reasoning, and strategic decision-making. We identified challenges in connecting abstra...

items.title: Visualizing Anisotropic Charge Transport in CrSBr using Bias-Dependent Kelvin Probe Force Microscopy
items.abstract: Anisotropic semiconductors offer unique opportunities for next-generation electronics due to their direction-dependent transport. However, conventional electrical measurements provide only spatially averaged characteristics. Here, we employ bias-dependent Kelvin probe force microscopy (KPFM) to directly visualize the response of CrSBr under different electrical bias configurations. Spatially resolved KPFM maps reveal highly distinct, crystallographic-direction-dependent potential profiles. To elucidate this behavior, we employ anisotropic transport simulations that capture the charge transport and electric-field distributions in CrSBr. The close agreement between experiment and simulation provides a unified picture of anisotropic charge transport and bias-induced potential redistribution. Our experiments further reveal a boundary-associated redistribution of the transport field when bias...

items.title: Streaming Virtual Metrology via Lightweight Adaptation under Temporal Distribution Shifts
items.abstract: Virtual metrology (VM) aims to estimate costly or delayed metrology variables from heterogeneous sensor signals and in-line measurements, and it acts as a critical component of semiconductor manufacturing. While recent data-driven models have improved VM accuracy, most are trained in batch settings and assume stationary data distributions. In practice, however, production environments evolve continuously due to equipment degradation, process adjustments, and maintenance events, making conventional batch-trained VM models difficult to maintain under temporal distribution shifts. In this work, we propose GRAPE (Global Regression with Adaptive Prediction Enhancement), a practical online learning framework for VM in evolving wafer-processing environments. GRAPE integrates a stable global predictor based on interpretable representations with two lightweight streaming adapters that correct fea...

items.title: A Mixed-Precision CNN-LSTM Accelerator Featuring Long-Kernel Memory Reuse and Dynamic Quantization for Sleep Staging
items.abstract: This letter presents a mixed-precision CNN-LSTM accelerator for EEG-based sleep staging. To efficiently execute long temporal convolutions, a serpentine dataflow propagates activations between neighboring processing elements, reducing memory accesses by 6.2 times and 2.25 times compared with output- and weight-stationary dataflows, respectively. A hybrid quantization scheme applies runtime dynamic quantization to the LSTM and MLP layers and assigns mixed precision on a layer-by-layer basis, reducing model size by 4.16 times. Combined with a bit-flexible MAC architecture and channel-grouped memory scheduling, the accelerator supports INT2/4/8/16 inference. Fabricated in 65 nm CMOS, the accelerator consumes 0.40 mW and achieves a 258 times speedup over an iso-frequency 32b RISC-V processor. items.title: Electronic liquid crystals and superconductivity from doping a moiré Mott insulator
items.abstract: Electronic liquid crystals, such as stripe phases and nematics, are self-organized states of matter with spontaneously broken rotational symmetry. They are expected to emerge in a doped Mott insulator as a compromise between short- and long-range Coulomb interactions, and are believed to be intimately connected to the emergence of high temperature superconductivity either as a competing order or an intertwined order. Moiré semiconductors provide a controllable platform to explore the relationship between stripe phases and superconductivity near a Mott insulator. Here we report the generic appearance of stripe phases in a doped moiré Mott insulator and the observation of a stripe to-superconductor quantum phase transition in twisted bilayer WSe2. items.title: Coherent Optical Control of a Single Donor Electron Spin
items.abstract: Coherent spin--photon interfaces for scalable quantum networks require bright optical transitions, long-lived spin coherence, and complete coherent spin control. Donor spins in direct-bandgap semiconductors combine strong donor-bound exciton transitions with a potentially nuclear-spin-free environment. However, coherent control of an individual optically active donor spin has remained elusive. Here, we demonstrate coherent optical control of a single Cl donor electron spin in ZnSe. Resonant excitation reveals spin relaxation dynamics and measures spin coherence through coherent population trapping (CPT). Off-resonant ultrafast pulses are implemented to drive spin Rabi oscillations and demonstrate Ramsey interference. Multiple dark resonances in the CPT spectrum further reveal hyperfine coupling between the electron and the I=3/2 Cl nucleus. Together, these results demonstrate the first c...

items.abstract: The drift-diffusion equations are the fundamental building block for the modeling, design, and optimization of modern semiconductor devices. Solutions of the drift-diffusion equations rarely give way to analytical forms, and exhibit strong nonlinearity, with the solutions ranging over several orders of magnitude. These attributes have led to research into numerical solvers, and while many commercial Technology Computer Aided Design (TCAD) packages now exist, they may require long simulation times, exhibit sensitivity to initial guesses, and rely on mesh generation. Further, these solvers are not well suited for inverse problems where the design parameters of a device are retrieved from its desired functional characteristics. To address all these challenges, this work demonstrates the usage of Physics Informed Neural Networks for the Drift-diffusion (PINND) equations with errors comparabl...

items.title: Online Open-World Wafer Defect Discovery using Hyperdimensional Computing
items.abstract: Conventional wafer defect analysis relies on offline, closed-world classifiers that fail to detect novel, unseen defect signatures emerging during continuous semiconductor manufacturing. To address this, we propose WaferHDC, an online open-world wafer defect discovery framework based on hyperdimensional computing (HDC). The memory-centric architecture of WaferHDC enables rapid anomaly detection and grouping of recurring failures into compact hypervector representations. This allows the memory space to dynamically scale with new defect modes without retraining a static classifier or archiving entire raw wafer history. WaferHDC first models normal spatial distributions, then dynamically groups recurring failures into persistent defect memory without labels or predefined class counts. It outperforms the strongest online baseline by 13.3 p.p. in adjusted Rand index and 10.5 p.p. in normalize...

items.title: Trapping of nanofabricated SiO$_2$ high-aspect-ratio discs in an optical lattice
items.abstract: We describe the nanofabrication and loading of lithographically patterned, high aspect ratio $10$ $μ$m diameter silicon dioxide discs with thickness of $400$ nm into an optical standing wave trap in vacuum. We obtain motional spectra of the center of mass motion of the discs using a combination of interferometric and imaging methods. The method is capable of high-efficiency loading and optical trapping using small numbers of objects, of the order of a few particles, with customized geometries and sizes compatible with wafer scale nanofabrication methods. Disc-like particles in optical traps have been identified as promising candidates for detectors of high frequency gravitational waves or as sensitive accelerometers.

items.title: Residual AM and PM Noise of Selected X-Band Amplifiers
items.abstract: In microwave systems design, amplitude modulation (AM) noise is often ignored relative to phase modulation (PM) noise. However, in high-performance applications requiring ultra-low PM noise, AM noise becomes a critical limiting factor due to AM-to-PM conversion mechanisms. Because AM noise specifications are rarely, if ever, provided for commercial microwave components, this study characterizes the residual AM and PM noise of several 10 GHz amplifiers. We present performance data for various Heterojunction Bipolar Transistor (HBT) amplifier designs and demonstrate the noise reduction achieved through power-summed configurations. For example, a discrete-die GaAs HBT amplifier achieves residual PM noise below $-160$ dBrad$^2$/Hz and AM noise of approximately $-155$ dB/Hz at a 1 kHz offset in a quad power-summed configuration. items.title: Hierarchical Fourier Phase Projection for Local Electronic Observables
items.abstract: In this letter, we develop hierarchical Fourier phase projection (HPP) for the calculation of local electronic observables. The method couples the spatial decay of the density matrix with a hierarchy of Fourier probes, improving accuracy through refinement, and making use of all previously evaluated responses. The variation in the calculated observables during the refinement process carries information on the residual error. We use a locality-based model to estimate the error from these changes with no extra probing calculations. In particular, we demonstrate the method for electron densities and nonlocal pseudopotential forces for fixed Kohn-Sham Hamiltonians of semiconductors, metals and thermally perturbed silica. The convergence is significantly accelerated by the spatial decay of the density matrix, especially if the density matrix is short-ranged. The number of probes necessary to...

items.title: Uncertainty and Business-Aware Remaining Useful Life Estimation for Semiconductor Manufacturing
items.abstract: Remaining Useful Life (RUL) estimates guide maintenance in semiconductor manufacturing, where a late intervention can disrupt production but an early one discards usable equipment life. A single prediction does not express the uncertainty needed to choose between these outcomes. We combine Deep Learning (DL) sequence models with Simoultaneous Quantile Regression (SQR) to estimate RUL at selectable quantile levels, and evaluate maintenance decisions using Unexpected Breaks (UB), Unexploited Lifetime (UL), and a cost-weighted objective. On the $F_1$ fault mode of the 2018 PHM Data Challenge (PHM18) ion-milling dataset, we compare recurrent, Transformer, and State Space Models (SSM) architectures. Diagonal State Spaced (S4D) gives the strongest overall RUL accuracy across the evaluated quantiles. Varying the quantile and maintenance window exposes the trade-off between failure risk and earl...

items.title: Transport-Noise and Optical Witnesses of Electronic Multipartite Entanglement
items.abstract: Entanglement among particles distinguishes correlated quantum materials from conventional metals and semiconductors. Experimentally certifying intrinsic entanglement among interacting electrons in materials is important not only for classifying states of matter, but also for developing material-based quantum technologies. Here, we introduce a transport protocol for witnessing multipartite entanglement from the equilibrium current-noise spectrum, measured directly or reconstructed from optical conductivity. The appropriately integrated, symmetrized, and projected noise spectrum obeys an upper bound derived from microscopic model parameters. Unlike witnesses based on localized spins, our framework applies to general electronic states without requiring magnetic moments and remains invariant under single-particle basis transformations. items.title: DACRI: Decision-Aware Causal Intervention Ranking for Critical Supply Chains
items.abstract: Detecting or attributing a supply-chain disruption is not the same as selecting the intervention that maximizes recoverable net value. We present CriticalSCM-Bench v1, a controlled synthetic benchmark with causal ground truth, paired factual/counterfactual rollouts, and an explicit net-value objective. Relative to a full-information train-selected static benchmark, LambdaMART improves median normalized net value by 5.7--16.2\%, with paired statistical support on the semiconductor and critical-material archetypes but not on digital infrastructure. On digital infrastructure, a domain-informed constant-buffer policy remains stronger, showing that greater model complexity is not uniformly justified. Across partial and delayed settings, LambdaMART retains 33--75\% of full-clamp value. Stress tests further show that intervention fidelity, timing, cost, and held-out disruptions can alter policy...

items.title: Who Needs DRAM? We Have Fiber
items.abstract: The rising pressure on DRAM availability and contract pricing reflects generative AI's massive high-performance memory requirements. This pressure is heavily compounded by hyperscale data center expansion, which now consumes a significant portion of global DRAM output. In this work, we propose a new architecture, Fiber Memory, which reimagines the role of optical fiber in a hyperscale data center, deploying it as an active, recirculating delay-line memory for immutable data, such as large language model weights. We present a hybrid data- and pipeline-parallel optical broadcast delay-line memory architecture that accounts for fiber's physical realities. By incorporating space-division multiplexed multi-core fibers, passive optical tap-and-amplify interfaces, co-packaged optics, and centralized in-ring 3R (re-amplify, reshape, retime) regeneration, our case study evaluation suggests that F...

items.title: Bright and Dark Excitons in CrSBr: Local Ligand-Field Character and Band-Coherent Optical Selection Rules
items.abstract: Magnetic van der Waals semiconductors such as CrSBr host an intricate exciton landscape. Quasiparticle self-consistent GW theory with electron-hole ladder vertex corrections (QSGWc) has established the gap and the character of the bright XA (1.34 eV) and XB (1.8 eV) excitons. Why these bright excitons coexist, within a few tens of meV, with companions orders of magnitude darker has remained unexplained. Here we show that brightness is fixed by a symmetry of the structure: a mirror-glide exchanges the two Cr atoms of each layer, every exciton has a definite parity under it, and bright and dark partners are its even and odd members. The even sector carries the b-axis dipole; the odd sector is suppressed by about three orders of magnitude. The dark partners of XA and XB occupy the same region of k-space as the bright states, and dark states such as the one at 1.50 eV are dipole-forbidden by...

items.title: Transmon Phase Gates Controlled by Superconducting Soliton DAC
items.abstract: We introduce a superconducting digital-to-analog converter (DAC) that filters control noise, provides native multiplexing, performs quantum gates in nanoseconds, and can be controlled by CMOS. This is achieved by transducing a trapezoidal drive pulse into a superconducting soliton, which is then held in the DAC load loop, applying flux to a mutually-coupled superconducting qubit or gate coupler. The analog flux output by the DAC can be easily controlled by varying the soliton hold time, or with a DC-biased tunable DAC-qubit coupler, allowing the DAC to perform a fixed-time, high-fidelity gate that's robust to fabrication variance or flux offsets in the quantum circuit. Our initial demonstration shows that the DAC can successfully perform 5.6 ns S-gates on transmons. We measure the DAC-induced quantum state excitation probability per gate to be 0.05%, and find that the DAC-induced relaxat...

items.title: Controllable Quantum Spin Hall Phases in Bi$_2$Te$_3$-Family van der Waals Heterobilayers
items.abstract: The tunability and control of topological edge/surface states are crucial for the development of new device applications. In this work, by combining first-principles calculations and Wannier-based tight-binding methods, we show the emergence of quantum spin Hall phases in van der Waals heterostructures formed by stacking two trivial quintuple layers from the Bi$_2$Te$_3$ family. We demonstrate the tunability of the edge states under interlayer strain and external electric field effects, suggesting the possibility of switching topological edge states on/off by external control. Additionally, the quantum spin Hall edge channels remain robust against interlayer twist, highlighting their stability against external perturbations. Our results provide a new way to create and manipulate two-dimensional topological phases in systems based on Bi$_2$Te$_3$ family, which can be valuable for practica...

items.title: Coexistence of Donor and Acceptor Hydrogen States in n-Type InN
items.abstract: Hydrogen often exhibits amphoteric behavior in semiconductors, but its role is in n-type InN remains unresolved. Wurtzite InN is a narrow-gap semiconductor with high electron mobility and is therefore attractive for high-speed electronics and optoelectronic applications. Here we use hard x-ray photoemission spectroscopy (HAXPES) to probe hydrogen-related electronic structure in as-grown and post-annealed InN thin films prepared at different grown temperatures. Post annealing, which reduces the concentration of hydrogen impurities in the films, shifts the core-level spectra toward lower binding energy, consistent with a chemical-potential shift associated with the passivation of electron carriers.
